art.title: Saint Apollonia Destroys a Pagan Idol
art.why: Why Rome called Christians 'atheists': they refused the city's gods. Apollonia was martyred at Alexandria c. 249 (the legend of her smashing an idol is later).

art.title: The Martyrdom of Saint Gennaro
art.why: A martyred bishop (Januarius, bishop of Benevento, d. c. 305). No NGA Polycarp.

art.title: Martyrdom of Saint Margaret
art.why: A young woman kneeling before the crowd and the sword. No NGA Perpetua; Margaret's story is largely legend: say so.

art.title: Saint Paul and a Group of Worshippers
art.why: A small company of ordinary believers at prayer under the apostle: the 'resident aliens' as a community. Paul holds the sword of his own martyrdom in Rome.

art.title: The Martyrdom of Saint Lawrence
art.why: Lawrence, deacon of Rome, killed in Valerian's persecution (258): the lecture's own period. The gridiron is the later tradition: note it.

art.title: Saint Sebastian
art.why: For 'myths of martyrdom': Sebastian's arrows are the famous image, but his earliest account says he survived them and was later beaten to death; most of his story is later legend. A test case for the session.

art.title: The Exaltation of the True Cross
art.why: The cross raised in a classical city: Christianity's public triumph after Constantine. No NGA Constantine or Chi-Rho. The gallery's description does not name Helena: describe only the cross, the kneeling man, the two women and the angels.

music.why: The hymn of the great company of the faithful, for the first session on the martyrs.
A coronation anthem: the Church's new alliance with power, and its danger.

flags: Candida Moss, Ste. Croix, Barnes and Open Doors figures: our own words, cited.
Session 1 compare (Tacitus) and Pliny are point-backs only.
Saints' legends on the paintings (Apollonia's idol, Lawrence's gridiron, Sebastian's arrows, Margaret) must be marked as later tradition.
